overview: Prospective observational comparison of residents who take part in monthly video review coaching and residents who do not, over the 2027 to 2028 academic year in one general surgery programme.
population: All 14 general surgery residents in the programme in July 2027; residents who leave the programme are followed until they leave.
exposure: Monthly video review coaching: the resident and a consultant coach review a filmed laparoscopic cholecystectomy or appendicectomy for about 45 minutes. Participation is voluntary and recorded at each session.
procedures: Each resident films one laparoscopic cholecystectomy in July to September 2027 and one in April to June 2028. Videos are edited to the critical steps and rated independently by two consultants who do not coach that resident, blind to coaching status and to timing. Study videos are stored separately from training records, never used in assessment, and deleted after rating.

outcomes.name: Change in operative skill
outcomes.measure: Mean of two blinded raters' global rating scale scores (5 to 25) at the end minus the start of the year
outcomes.timing: Start and end of the academic year
outcomes.why: Reliable blinded measure of the skill coaching aims to improve.

outcomes.name: Intraoperative autonomy
outcomes.measure: Attending rating on a four-level autonomy scale after each cholecystectomy
outcomes.why: Matters to residents and supervisors; unblinded, so secondary.

outcomes.name: Coaching sessions attended
outcomes.why: Describes the dose of coaching actually received.

outcomes.name: Resident concern about filming
outcomes.measure: Two-item anonymous rating of worry about video use
outcomes.timing: Start and end of the year
outcomes.why: Filming must not become a source of fear.

feasibility: Filming already happens; rating two edited videos per resident takes about 12 minutes each for two raters, about 11 hours in total; coaching uses the two volunteer consultants' existing time.
biasMitigation: Raters blind to coaching status and timing
Adjustment for baseline score and training year
Participation recorded prospectively rather than recalled

biasFlags.label: Self-selection into coaching
biasFlags.note: Adjustment for baseline score reduces but cannot remove it.

biasFlags.label: Small sample
biasFlags.note: Fourteen residents give an imprecise estimate.

flags: Two covariates only: baseline score and training year
parsimony.simplestPath: One programme, one index operation, two videos per resident, two blinded raters.

theoreticalFramework: None; the question is an empirical comparison and no educational framework changes the measurement.
summary: One-year prospective comparison with a blinded primary outcome and strict rules on video use.
